headline: Bank of Canada hikes to 2.5%; oil jumps to $102 as Fed looms
summary: The Bank of Canada raised its key rate by a quarter point to 2.5% at 9:45 a.m., its first hike in more than three years, and said another may follow; the loonie slipped about 0.3% to 71.15 U.S. cents as U.S. crude jumped 2.5% to about $102.40. An hour into trading, U.S. stocks are barely moving before the Fed's 2 p.m. decision: the S&P 500 is up 0.1% near 7,733, the Nasdaq flat near 26,470 and the TSX down 0.1% near 36,134, with memory-chip stocks up after SK Hynix's huge quarter while Tesla (-2%) and Meta (-1%) lag. Crypto is flat: bitcoin gave back an early push above $81,000 and sits near $80,500 (up 0.4% in 24 hours, down 3.4% this week), ether is about $2,330, total crypto value is about $2.71 trillion and Fear & Greed is a neutral 51.

crypto.label: Cautious
crypto.why: Bitcoin briefly topped $81,000 but slipped back to about $80,500, just under the roughly $81,500 average price ETF buyers paid, and Fear & Greed is a neutral 51 ahead of the Fed.

stocks.label: Mixed
stocks.why: Chip stocks are up on SK Hynix's results, but the indexes are flat, oil is back above $102, the 10-year yield is just over 5% and the Fed plus Microsoft and Alphabet results are still to come.

drivers.title: Bank of Canada hikes to 2.5% and leaves the door open to more
drivers.detail: The bank raised its rate a quarter point to 2.5%, as expected, saying high energy prices risk spreading into wider inflation (3.2% in September, above its 1%-3% band); it now sees inflation at 3.5% by year-end and about 3% through most of 2027, and Governor Macklem said further hikes are possible but it will move carefully, per BNN Bloomberg. Some economists opposed the move because core inflation is near 2% and the job market is weak, and the loonie is down about 0.3% to 71.15 U.S. cents on our feed.
drivers.assets: Canadian banks, the loonie, mortgages, TSX

drivers.title: AI chip trade: SK Hynix lifts memory stocks
drivers.detail: SK Hynix reported a 632% jump in quarterly operating profit and a roughly $75 billion shareholder-return plan, lifting Micron (about +4% before the open) and Western Digital (+4.5%), per Coinpaper, while Broadcom is up about 1% on our feed after a $63 billion bank financing for AI computing power. Worries about debt-funded data-centre spending have not gone away (CoreWeave bond yields are near 15%), so Microsoft's and Alphabet's spending plans after today's close matter a lot.

crypto.name: Bitcoin
crypto.move: Up 0.4% over 24h but down 3.4% this week, at about $80,500 (down 3.5% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Bitcoin rose about 2% to just above $81,000 early Wednesday as an Asian chip rally spilled into crypto, then slipped about $1,000 back to roughly $80,500, near Tuesday's close, as oil jumped and traders waited for the Fed, per CoinDesk. U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs (funds that hold the coin for stock-market investors) took in about $110 million Monday and about $176 million Tuesday, per Bloomingbit, after roughly $943 million of outflows over the prior three sessions, but Strategy said it bought no bitcoin in the week to Oct. 25. The Fed is expected to hold at 3.75%-4%; CoinDesk notes that if three or more officials vote to hike, the dollar could jump and weigh on bitcoin. Galaxy's Alex Thorn argues bitcoin likely bottomed in June under $58,000, and Bitwise raised its long-term forecast to $1.6 million by 2036, while tech investor Jason Calacanis expects a fall to $57,000 within 12 months.
crypto.meaning: Glassnode estimates ETF buyers and corporate treasuries bought, on average, between about $80,000 and $81,500, so bitcoin is sitting right around the price where many big holders break even; staying under it can prompt more selling. Two straight days of ETF inflows are an early sign dip buyers are returning, but two days is not yet a trend.

outlook.bullCase: A calm Fed on Oct. 28, ETF inflows returning and a U.S.–Iran deal could lift it back above $82,000–$82,500 (Thursday's lost floor), putting $85,000–$87,000 back in view.
outlook.bearCase: A daily close below $79,000, more ETF outflows, a hawkish Fed or a U.S. strike on Iran could extend the slide toward $77,600 (Glassnode's estimate of the average holder's cost) and then $75,000.
outlook.watch: Whether it can close back above $80,000, whether ETF inflows continue, the Fed decision and Warsh press conference on Oct. 28, whether Strategy resumes buying (its results are Oct. 29), and about $11 billion of bitcoin options expiring Oct. 30.

crypto.name: Ethereum
crypto.move: Flat over 24h (+0.1%) and down 5.5% this week, at about $2,330 (down 13% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Ether rose about 2% to roughly $2,360 early Wednesday with the rest of the market, per CoinDesk, but has slipped back to about $2,330 on our feed. It is still under the $2,400 level that had supported it for about a week, and ether ETFs (over $1.1 billion out in October, their worst month this year, per Crypto Briefing) lost about $89 million Monday and about $60 million more Tuesday, led by BlackRock's fund, per Bloomingbit, even as bitcoin ETFs drew money back in.
crypto.meaning: Ether is lagging bitcoin because big investors keep pulling money from the ETFs. Until those flows turn, rallies may be harder to sustain.

outlook.bearCase: A break below $2,290 (Saturday's low) with continued ETF outflows and more forced selling could send it toward $2,150–$2,200, and a broader risk-off turn could push it lower.
outlook.watch: Daily ether ETF flows, the $2,300 and $2,400 levels, the ETH/BTC ratio, and any new Glamsterdam upgrade timeline.

crypto.name: Hyperliquid
crypto.move: Up 0.8% over 24h and down 1.8% this week, at about $79.80 (down 12% over 30 days; about 19% below its record near $98)
crypto.why: Hyperliquid runs a popular exchange for perpetual futures (bets on prices that never expire) on its own blockchain, and HYPE is the top trending coin on CoinGecko. It rose nearly 6% to about $81 early Wednesday, per CoinDesk, before easing back below $80, one of the best performers among large coins, per CoinDesk, moving with a broad crypto bounce rather than on a single headline we could find. The 24-hour range on our feed ran from about $77 to $82.
crypto.meaning: HYPE tends to move more than bitcoin in both directions because it is tied to trading activity on its exchange. A rebound toward the high-$80s would need busier trading and a calm Fed; it remains a higher-risk holding than bitcoin or ether.

outlook.bullCase: Holding above about $80 with rising exchange volume and a steady broader market could lift it toward $85–$90 and a retest of the record near $98.
outlook.bearCase: A hawkish Fed or a renewed crypto sell-off could send it back to the $75–$77 area where it traded earlier this week, and below that toward about $70.
outlook.watch: The $80 level, Hyperliquid trading volume and open interest, and bitcoin's reaction to the Fed decision.

crypto.name: Bitway
crypto.move: Up 18.7% over 24h on our feed (largely a rebound from a sharp dip) and up 9.9% this week, at about $1.77 (up 35% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Bitway is the top 100's biggest 24-hour gainer, though much of that gain came from recovering a sharp dip, with no specific news trigger we could find either way; it had already fallen about 25% on Oct. 15 when a hot U.S. inflation report hit crypto, and slid from above $2.60 to about $1.70 in the week to Oct. 24, per CoinMarketCap's update page. Trackers say the top 100 wallets hold almost all of the supply, which makes sharp moves like this more likely, and about 101.6 million BTW (roughly 1% of the 10 billion total, about $175 million at today's price) is due to unlock on Nov. 2, per CryptoTicker. An unlock is when tokens held back for insiders or ecosystem funds become free to sell. Big swings in both directions are typical of a thinly traded token after a crash.
crypto.meaning: This is a high-risk token whose price can swing tens of percent in a day, with conflicting public data on how many tokens are actually circulating. Holders face more supply coming each month through 2030, and whether the Nov. 2 tranche goes to early backers (more likely to sell) or ecosystem pools is disputed between trackers.

outlook.bullCase: If the price holds above roughly $1.60 and the market absorbs the Nov. 2 unlock without heavy selling, a push back toward $2.00–$2.60 (mid-October levels) is possible.
outlook.bearCase: If large holders sell into the rebound or around the unlock, the price could fall back toward $1.20–$1.00, where it bottomed during the recent dip.
outlook.watch: Whether $1.60 holds, large wallet transfers to exchanges, trading volume, and price action around the Nov. 2 08:00 UTC unlock.

crypto.name: LayerZero
crypto.move: Flat over 24h (-0.2%) and down 17% this week, at about $1.69 (up 5% over 30 days)
crypto.why: LayerZero runs a messaging system that lets apps send tokens and data between different blockchains, and ZRO is its token. It has bounced about 4% over the past 24 hours but is still down about 15% this week, and we found no fresh headline behind Monday's drop. It has been weak since an Oct. 20 token unlock (about 6% of supply), after which roughly 9.7 million ZRO was reportedly moved to big exchanges, per CoinMarketCap's AI news summary; an unlock is when tokens held back for insiders become free to sell. The project announced on Oct. 20 that its Zero mainnet and lzATLAS launch, which adds a buy-and-burn of ZRO funded by fees, is planned for Nov. 30, per TokenPost.
crypto.meaning: Recurring unlocks keep adding supply that early holders can sell, which has outweighed upgrade news so far this month. The Nov. 30 launch is the project's main potential catalyst, but a fee-funded burn only helps the price if the network earns meaningful fees.

outlook.bullCase: If selling from the unlock runs out and bitcoin steadies above $80,000, ZRO could bounce back toward $1.80–$2.00, where it traded last week.
outlook.bearCase: Continued exchange deposits from large wallets or a weaker crypto market after the Fed could push it below $1.60 toward about $1.40–$1.50.
outlook.watch: Large ZRO transfers to exchanges, whether $1.60 holds, the next monthly unlock date, and any update on the Nov. 30 Zero mainnet launch.

crypto.name: XRP
crypto.move: Flat over 24h (-0.3%) and down 3.0% this week, at about $1.31 (down 14% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Ripple, the company most closely tied to XRP, won final approval from the U.S. bank regulator (the OCC) for a national trust bank that will manage the reserves behind its RLUSD stablecoin and hold crypto for institutional clients, per CoinDesk. XRP rose about 1% on the news, per Investing.com, but is still around $1.30. Separately, Franklin Templeton last week put about $150 million more of its tokenized money-market fund onto the XRP Ledger, per CoinDesk. Robinhood also said it will offer RLUSD to its customers, per CoinDesk.
crypto.meaning: A federal bank charter gives Ripple's stablecoin and custody business more credibility with banks, but neither the charter nor tokenized funds require anyone to buy XRP, so the price link is indirect. XRP is still down about 15% over the past month, so this is a small bounce inside a larger slide.

outlook.bullCase: More tokenized-fund news and a steadier bitcoin above $80,000 could lift XRP back toward $1.40–$1.45.
outlook.bearCase: If bitcoin loses $80,000 again or the wider market turns risk-off after the Fed, XRP could slip back toward $1.20–$1.25.
outlook.watch: Whether XRP can hold gains on the bank-charter news, RLUSD growth, bitcoin's hold on $80,000, and the Oct. 28 Fed decision.

crypto.name: MemeCore
crypto.move: Up 5.6% over 24h and up 44% this week, at about $1.12 (down 6% over 30 days)
crypto.why: MemeCore, a blockchain built around meme coins, was the biggest decliner among about 90 large coins tracked by TokenPost on Sunday morning, falling to about $0.92; it has since bounced to about $1.08, up about 14% over 24 hours and the biggest gainer in the top 100, with no specific trigger reported either way. About 56 million new M tokens (roughly 2.8% of circulating supply, about $50 million, per CoinDesk) unlock on Nov. 1, which adds potential selling pressure.

outlook.bullCase: If the sell-off was one large holder exiting and the broader market steadies, it could rebound toward $1.05–$1.15, where it traded earlier this week.
outlook.bearCase: More large-wallet selling or selling ahead of the Nov. 1 unlock could push it toward $0.75–$0.80, its lows from mid-October.
outlook.watch: Large transfers to exchanges from top wallets, the Nov. 1 unlock, and whether the project explains the drop.

crypto.name: Zcash
crypto.move: Down 0.5% over 24h and down 1.1% this week, at about $1,273 (down 20% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Traders had been positioning for the NU7 upgrade, which developers scheduled for about 7:50 p.m. ET on Nov. 5; it cuts block times from 75 to 25 seconds and sends 60% of fees to a reserve. Futures open interest (the value of open bets) had risen about 19–24% and two large traders reportedly opened about $37.6 million of 10x leveraged longs. Those leveraged bets have been unwinding: CoinDesk flagged ZEC among the coins where bullish traders were closing positions, and it noted an 8% drop in open interest Friday. After Monday's sell-off, ZEC led the large coins overnight, rising about 8% to about $1,320, per CoinDesk, and was still near $1,300 at 7:23 a.m., per CoinDesk, before slipping to about $1,273 on our feed, as traders re-position ahead of the upgrade.
crypto.meaning: Much of this month's rally was driven by borrowed money, and this week shows how fast that can reverse. Upgrade dates often bring 'buy the rumour, sell the news' behaviour, so swings both ways are likely into Nov. 5.

outlook.bullCase: Holding above $1,300 and renewed interest as the upgrade nears could bring it back to the $1,375 resistance and, beyond that, the September high near $1,700.
outlook.bearCase: Losing $1,180 would erase the October breakout and could send it toward about $1,000–$1,120, near its 50-day average.
outlook.watch: The $1,180 level, funding rates and open interest, ETF flows, and any upgrade delay.

crypto.name: Solana
crypto.move: Flat over 24h (+0.2%) and down 5.5% this week, at about $100.60 (down 16% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Solana completed its Alpenglow upgrade, a major overhaul aimed at much faster transaction finality (the point at which a payment can't be reversed), according to CoinDesk. The price has moved with the market rather than rallying on the news, and it slipped under $100 Saturday morning as bitcoin's break below $80,000 triggered forced selling across crypto, briefly tested $100 again in Asian trading Monday, and it is about $99.21 early Tuesday, just below that line.
crypto.meaning: A smooth Alpenglow launch is a meaningful technical milestone, but the market is treating it as already expected. The first days after a big upgrade are when problems usually show up, so stability matters more than headlines.

outlook.bullCase: A trouble-free upgrade and stronger crypto risk appetite could lift SOL back toward $115–$120.
outlook.bearCase: Any outage or bug after the upgrade, or bitcoin staying below $80,000, could push SOL toward $90.
outlook.watch: Whether SOL regains $100, network stability after Alpenglow, bitcoin's $80,000 level, and Solana ETF flows.

stocks.name: Celestica
stocks.move: Closed up about 12% on Tuesday after Monday evening's results, the TSX's top gainer, per Yahoo Finance (our live feed does not track CLS)
stocks.why: Celestica, a Toronto-based company that builds servers, networking switches and other hardware for AI data centres, reported third-quarter revenue of $5.83 billion, up 83% from a year earlier, and adjusted earnings of $3.30 a share, above its own guidance, per its filing. It raised its 2026 forecast to $21.0 billion of revenue and $11.55 a share (from $20.5 billion and $11.30), and gave a first 2027 outlook of $40 billion of revenue and $21.50 a share, nearly double this year. One soft spot: it cut its 2026 free-cash-flow forecast to $460 million from $600 million as it spends more to expand capacity.
stocks.meaning: The 2027 forecast says Celestica's biggest customers (large cloud companies) expect to keep spending heavily on AI hardware next year, a counterpoint to last week's worries about AI returns. The stock has already run up a lot on this story, so expectations are high and it is very sensitive to any sign that AI spending is slowing.

outlook.bullCase: If the premarket jump holds through the open and Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon confirm big AI spending plans this week, the stock could push toward fresh highs.
outlook.bearCase: If the broader AI-chip sell-off resumes, or investors focus on the lower cash-flow forecast and heavy spending, the opening pop could fade back toward Monday's close.
outlook.watch: Where it opens Tuesday in Toronto and New York, management's comments on customer concentration and capacity, and Big Tech capital-spending guidance on Oct. 28–29.

stocks.move: Down 0.9% at about $614 in morning trading, after falling 1.6% Tuesday; down about 12% since last Wednesday
stocks.why: Nvidia said Tuesday it will put $3 billion into Meta's $35 billion share sale and expand work on Meta's Muse AI models, per Yahoo Finance. Meta launched a $35 billion share sale Monday to pay for AI data centres: about $22.5 billion of common stock sold through forward agreements and $12.5 billion of three-year mandatory convertible preferred shares (which turn into common stock later), plus a planned program of up to $60 billion of non-voting Class C shares starting in early 2027, per ZeroHedge and KuCoin News. Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom indicated interest in buying up to $5 billion. Shares rose before the bell, fell to about $629 after the open, recovered to about $648, before closing near the day's low at about $631. Last week's results beat forecasts, but the $135–$145 billion spending plan, roughly -$2.1 billion of free cash flow and a $9.9 billion legal charge sank the stock 7% Thursday. Meta priced the common-stock part at $625 a share (40 million shares, about $25 billion), with the convertibles set to turn into stock at about $734, per Bank of Vol.
stocks.meaning: Selling new shares spreads the company's profits over more stock (dilution), and the scale here is unusual for a company that was buying back shares. Chip-maker interest shows suppliers want to keep Meta spending, but it also feeds 'circular financing' worries, where AI buyers and sellers fund each other.

outlook.bullCase: If the offering is absorbed smoothly and investors refocus on 26% revenue growth, it could recover toward $680–$700.
outlook.bearCase: Pressure from new supply, rising credit-risk pricing (its five-year credit default swaps are about double August's level, per ZeroHedge) or weak results from other Big Tech spenders could push it below $630 toward $600.
outlook.watch: The offering's final pricing, whether $630 holds, and Alphabet's and Microsoft's spending plans on Oct. 28.

stocks.name: Advanced Micro Devices
stocks.move: Up 0.4% at about $563 in morning trading, after Tuesday's 5.5% jump; about 15% below its 52-week high
stocks.why: AMD is among the day's biggest large-cap gainers as last week's AI-chip sell-off eases, helped by Anthropic's IPO filing and its large compute commitments, and it was named, along with Nvidia and Broadcom, as a possible buyer of up to $5 billion of Meta's new stock, per ZeroHedge and HDFC Sky. It fell 8.1% Thursday on doubts about AI spending returns and 'circular' financing worries, and trades at a high valuation, roughly 200 times its past year's earnings.
stocks.meaning: AMD has been one of the biggest AI winners of the past year, more than doubling from its low, so it swings hard when sentiment turns. Its own results on Nov. 3 are the next real test of whether AI chip demand is holding up.

outlook.bullCase: Strong Microsoft and Alphabet spending plans on Oct. 28 and solid guidance on Nov. 3 could lift it back toward $560–$600.
outlook.bearCase: If the AI-spending worry deepens, it could slide toward the $470–$480 area where it traded in late September.
outlook.watch: Chip-sector moves, Big Tech capital-spending guidance on Oct. 28–29, and AMD's Nov. 3 results.

stocks.name: Tesla
stocks.move: Down 2.0% at about $399 in morning trading, giving back part of Tuesday's 4.0% gain; about 20% below its 52-week high of about $499
stocks.why: Barclays analyst Dan Levy upgraded Tesla to Overweight (a buy-type rating) and raised his target to $450 from $370, citing a possible combination with SpaceX (both companies have set up exploratory committees), a turnaround in the car business and faster robotaxi progress, per Investing.com. Sell ratings on the stock are now at their lowest share in about 11 years after BNP Paribas and CLSA dropped negative calls last week, and Latvia became the tenth EU country to approve Tesla's Full Self-Driving software.
stocks.meaning: Two days of gains are driven by deal hopes and analyst upgrades rather than new sales numbers, so the stock is pricing in a SpaceX tie-up that has not been agreed. That makes it sensitive to any headline about the merger talks in either direction.

outlook.bullCase: Concrete progress on a SpaceX combination or more upgrades could carry it toward Barclays' $450 target.
outlook.bearCase: If merger talk cools or big-tech earnings disappoint, it could give back the two-day jump toward the $370–$390 area it held last week.
outlook.watch: Any statement from the SpaceX and Tesla committees, big-tech results on Oct. 28–29, and whether it holds above Monday's $391.62 close.

stocks.name: Broadcom
stocks.move: Up 1.1% at about $346 in morning trading, after Tuesday's 4.0% gain; still about 30% below its 52-week high of $495
stocks.why: Broadcom is rising with other chipmakers after Anthropic's IPO filing, which named it among the suppliers in more than $500 billion of compute commitments, per HDFC Sky, and banks including Bank of America, Citi and Morgan Stanley plus Blackstone lined up financing of roughly $60 billion or more for Anthropic's purchase of Broadcom-designed chips, per NewsBytes and earlier Bloomberg-sourced reports. It was also named as a possible buyer of Meta's new shares.
stocks.meaning: Broadcom designs custom AI chips for big customers, so a single deal of this size can shape its revenue for years; the financing removes some doubt about whether Anthropic can pay for it. The stock has fallen sharply from its highs on worries about how AI spending is funded, so it reacts strongly to news like this in either direction.

outlook.bullCase: If Big Tech's results on Oct. 28–29 confirm heavy AI spending and the Anthropic IPO goes smoothly, it could retake the $355–$375 range where it traded earlier this month.
outlook.bearCase: If worries about debt-funded AI spending return or the chip rebound fades, it could slip back toward $320, Friday's low area.
outlook.watch: Whether it holds above $335, Microsoft and Alphabet spending guidance on Oct. 28, Anthropic IPO pricing news, and the chip sector's next move.

stocks.name: Robinhood Markets
stocks.move: Fell about 6-8% before the open after third-quarter results, per CoinDesk and Yahoo Finance (our live feed does not track HOOD)
stocks.why: Robinhood earned $0.51 a share in the third quarter, short of the $0.55 analysts expected, and revenue of $1.42 billion, a record, was just under the roughly $1.43 billion forecast, per StockTwits via Yahoo Finance. The weak spot was crypto: crypto revenue fell about 55%, per CoinDesk, as retail crypto trading cooled with bitcoin stuck near $80,000, and TipRanks pointed to the weak crypto results as the main disappointment.
stocks.meaning: Robinhood's results are a real-time read on how much everyday investors are trading, and they say crypto enthusiasm among retail traders has faded since last year. For crypto holders it is a sign that demand is coming more from ETFs and institutions than from app traders; for the stock, growth now leans on stock and options trading, banking and prediction markets.

outlook.bullCase: If the drop is absorbed in regular trading and October crypto and options volumes (in its monthly metrics report) rebound, the stock could recover part of the loss.
outlook.bearCase: If selling extends after the open and Coinbase's results Thursday also show weak retail crypto trading, the stock could keep sliding as analysts cut estimates.
outlook.watch: How the stock trades after the 9:30 a.m. open, analyst target changes, Coinbase earnings on Oct. 29, and bitcoin's hold on $80,000.

stocks.name: Visa
stocks.move: Was down about 1.4% before the open after results, per StockTwits via Yahoo Finance (our live feed does not track V)
stocks.why: Visa's fiscal fourth-quarter revenue rose 13% to $12.1 billion and adjusted earnings rose 17% to $3.48 a share, ahead of the roughly $3.44 analysts expected, per AlphaStreet. Payments volume grew 9% and cross-border volume (spending outside a card's home country, a high-margin business) 14%. For fiscal 2027 it guided to revenue and earnings-per-share growth in the low double digits, per Reuters, which StockTwits notes disappointed some investors, and it raised its dividend 16% after buying back $4 billion of stock in the quarter.
stocks.meaning: The results show consumer spending, including travel, is holding up. The mild after-hours dip suggests the beat and a steady but unexciting 2027 outlook were largely priced in after October's roughly 11% run-up.

outlook.bullCase: If Wednesday's trading shakes off the after-hours dip and Mastercard's results confirm strong cross-border spending, the stock could retest its recent highs.
outlook.bearCase: If investors read the 2027 outlook as a slowdown, or UK card-fee legal claims and U.S. swipe-fee legislation gain traction, October's run-up could keep unwinding.
outlook.watch: Wednesday's regular-session reaction, Mastercard's results later this week, and any news on swipe-fee rules or the UK claims.

stocks.name: TD Bank
stocks.move: Down 0.3% at about C$176.10 after the Bank of Canada hike, just off Tuesday's record close of C$176.57; RBC is down 0.4% at about C$284.30
stocks.why: Canadian banks are slightly lower after the Bank of Canada raised its rate to 2.5% and said more hikes are possible. A modest hike tends to widen bank lending margins (the gap between what banks pay on deposits and earn on loans), but more hikes would squeeze borrowers and could raise loan losses. TD hit a record high earlier this week.
stocks.meaning: TD is near a record, so the next leg depends on a stable rate outlook and its next results. Bank stocks are a big part of many Canadian portfolios.

outlook.bullCase: A well-signalled path with no more than one more hike and calm credit markets could take TD through C$177 to new highs.
outlook.bearCase: Signs that the bank will keep hiking, raising fears for mortgage holders and loan losses, could pull it back to the C$167-C$170 area.
outlook.watch: Whether the bank signals one more hike or several, mortgage-renewal stress, and Canadian bank results in late November.
